scope_description.value: Full A-E design services for replacement of 12 substations (A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, K, L) within Building NH-95 at Naval Support Activity Hampton Roads, Norfolk, VA. Existing substations were beyond their useful life with leaking oil-filled transformers and obsolete breakers. Scope included: demolish existing switchgear and oil-filled transformers; provide new exterior pad-mounted transformers for each substation; provide service-entrance-rated double-ended switchboards with automatic transfer switches; modify existing primary and secondary ductbanks and manholes; architectural vault expansions (A&B: ~42'x19'; C/D/F: ~37'x11'); structural pile foundation for addition; fire protection modifications; mechanical ventilation; hazardous materials survey/abatement (lead paint, PCBs, asbestos); geotechnical investigation; civil site improvements; erosion and sediment control; arc flash/coordination studies; circuit trace drawings for all substations. Delivery method: Design-Bid-Build.
scope_description.quote: This project includes the complete design for the replacement of existing substations A, B, K and L. Substations A, B, K and L are beyond their useful life. The existing transformers are leaking oil and the existing breakers are no longer able to be purchased and replaced.

hazardous_materials_present.quote: Lead paint; Oil Filled Transformers; Asbestos Containing Ductbank and Manholes
hazardous_materials_present.notes: HazMat survey found: no ACM in sampled areas, but lead/cadmium/chromium in paint samples confirmed above laboratory MDL. PCBs not present in transformer oil (< 1 PPM). Fluorescent light tubes assumed mercury-containing.

building_construction_date.quote: Building NH-95 was constructed in the 1950s. There have been various additions to the building over the years.

corroboration.claim: Building NH-95 was constructed in the 1950s

geotechnical_findings.value: Site Class D; no liquefaction potential; soils are medium dense to very loose silty/clayey sands to 30 ft, clays/silts to ~65 ft, sands below. Groundwater 7–10 ft below grade. Helical piles recommended for building addition (30-kip capacity at 25 ft depth). Mildly corrosive soils.
geotechnical_findings.quote: Seismic Site Class D is expected to be appropriate for the project site based on this exploration and our past experience.

substation_equipment_summary.value: Substations A & B: 3000A, 208Y/120V services with 1000 kVA oil-filled transformers (existing), replaced with new exterior pad-mounted 1000 kVA transformers and 3000A double-ended switchboards. Substations K & L: 4000A, 480Y/277V services with 2500 kVA oil-filled transformers (existing), replaced with new exterior pad-mounted 2500 kVA transformers and 4000A double-ended switchboards with auto-throwover. Substations C-J: 8 substations with new exterior transformers and double-ended switchboards with redundancy. All switchboards are Square D/Schneider QED-2 or QED-6 construction with MasterPact MTZ circuit breakers.
